marker.contents: WordPress loader: hidden staged PHP restoration; add include detection

samples.identification: Concealed WordPress plugin restoring and evaluating an externally stored PHP stage
execution_trace: Registers all_plugins callback that unsets its own plugin_basename(__FILE__) entry, concealing the plugin from the admin inventory.

Registers plugins_loaded callback at priority zero. Reads source from a SysV shmop segment opened read-only. If absent or empty, connects using WordPress DB credentials, selects option_value, then base64-decodes and gzip-decompresses that value.

Sets an executable PHP target under WP_CONTENT_DIR/mu-plugins. If the file is absent, writes the selected source, applies mode 0644, and invalidates the PHP bytecode cache. Includes that same target immediately afterward. The mu-plugin location supplies subsequent WordPress activation.
The external source and existing target file are not present in the artifact. No decoded final stage is recoverable from its bytes. Encoding calls describe runtime staging, not an embedded payload.

The callback does not capture/global-declare table_prefix, so the DB fallback can fail or query an unintended options table in a normal WordPress closure scope. Shared-memory and filesystem availability also condition success. These limitations do not erase the explicit concealed staging/evaluation logic.
samples.reason: Concealment plus early executable restoration and immediate inclusion tips the judgment. No authorized maintenance context or disclosed repair interface accompanies the loader; the final stage remains unknown.
samples.coverage: Both existing hostile restoration findings and both suspicious findings retained. Added a same-variable check/write/include observation and hostile concealed-stage evaluation. Three hostile findings now span persistence and payload execution.

marker.contents: Chromium library: caller-driven recovery; retain suspicious bypass

samples.identification: chromium-crypto 0.5.3 Rust library from the tidy-browser workspace
execution_trace: Verified original crate hash, archive member list, Cargo.toml/Cargo.toml.orig, all seven source members and their facts. Cargo declares a library, build=false, and disables automatic binaries/examples/tests/benches. No executable/install entrypoint or opaque embedded executable is shipped.

Linux build(safe_storage, predicate) connects to the desktop Secret Service, unlocks/enumerates the default collection and caches caller-selected label secrets. decrypt receives ciphertext from its caller; v10 uses the public peanuts/saltysalt parameters, v11 uses the cached secret, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 derives an AES-CBC key, and padded decryption returns a String.

macOS obtains a caller-selected keyring entry secret, derives AES-CBC keys with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1/1003 iterations, decrypts caller-supplied bytes, and returns plaintext. Cookie mode can omit the first 32 plaintext bytes; Login mode returns the complete string.

Windows build accepts a caller-supplied Local State path, reads/parses JSON and decodes DPAPI/App-Bound keys. It can enable SeDebugPrivilege, enumerate lsass/winlogon, open and duplicate their tokens, impersonate SYSTEM, unwrap SYSTEM DPAPI, revert to the user for another DPAPI layer, and optionally unwrap Google Chromekey1 using CNG. Key-blob flags choose fixed AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, or CNG/XOR/AES-GCM derivation. decrypt returns caller-supplied cookie/login plaintext.

OpenProcess uses VM_READ access rights but the code does not call ReadProcessMemory or dump LSASS contents. Privilege enabling requires an eligible token; there is no demonstrated unprivileged-to-admin exploit. Impersonation guards revert context and close handles, which is ordinary resource cleanup.

Plain source and documented crypto formats explain the hex constants and Base64 handling. The library implements local caller-requested recovery, rather than a hidden collector. It has no profile-database sweep, background execution, persistence or external secret-transfer path in the reviewed source.
samples.reason: The public source-only library packaging, explicit recovery API and actual caller-driven return paths support BENIGN. SYSTEM token impersonation and App-Bound decryption remain suspicious dual-use capabilities. Authorization of a downstream consumer is unknown; the library alone does not demonstrate theft.
samples.coverage: Kept the complete App-Bound composite matcher at suspicious rather than hostile: it proves boundary crossing, not theft. Retained existing SYSTEM token and browser-key findings. Added eight distinct notable facts across crypto, keyring, D-Bus, privilege adjustment and process enumeration. Existing 27 boundary controls still pass.

marker.contents: SMA exploit: batch RCE/policy-read attempts; fix neutral trait placement

samples.identification: Standalone Python batch SMA wsproxy/Erlang exploit-attempt client
execution_trace: main reads and strips a local target list and maps exploit over a ThreadPoolExecutor of 50 workers. The referenced target-list file and claimed Shodan provenance are not supplied.

Each target first receives a JSON POST to /wsproxy requesting host 127.0.0.1, port 1050, secure=false. It then receives JSON node/cookie/message fields constructing os:cmd("id; uname -a") and os:cmd("cat /usr/local/extranet/etc/policy_file.xml"). urllib reads each response but exploit discards the returned bytes; only exceptions are printed.

This is not a complete WebSocket/Erlang exploit implementation: there is no HTTP Upgrade/WebSocket framing, Erlang distribution handshake, challenge authentication or ETF encoding. The cookie string is a placeholder-looking constant. The comments and CVE attribution are not verified evidence of success or authentic firmware secrets.

An offline replay with urlopen replaced by an in-memory stub confirmed exactly three POST requests and their source-derived payloads. No sample endpoint was contacted, no target list opened by main, and no local OS command executed. The replay is not evidence of successful remote execution.
There is no obfuscated embedded stage, remote credential decryption routine, local policy-file saving or separate exfiltration infrastructure in the artifact.
samples.reason: Batch targeting, internal-service pivot requests, OS reconnaissance commands and credential-bearing appliance policy retrieval form an offensive exploitation sequence. Its scale and sensitive target selection tip MALICIOUS without inventing deployment authorization. Operational effectiveness remains unproven.
samples.coverage: All three hostile attack patterns and policy-read suspicious finding retained. The bare policy path, generic Erlang os:cmd syntax and named-port assignment were relocated to their neutral subjects, preserving matchers and original scope at notable. Existing consumers follow the moves; the multi-app theft suppressor preserves its original path observation set.

severity_corrections: Rust package composite hostile -> suspicious: actual library demonstrates legitimate caller-driven local recovery with the exact matched token/CNG/DPAPI sequence; matcher retained. No package-name exclusion was added.
SMA policy path suspicious -> notable: a path alone proves neither access nor credential theft. The credential-read command and hostile read-through-exploit composite remain.
Erlang os:cmd syntax suspicious -> notable: ordinary Erlang administration can use this shell command syntax without an SMA exploit. Hostile composites still require appliance/proxy context.
Erlang-named port assignment suspicious -> notable: a source assignment proves no listening socket, connection or SSRF. The hostile contextual composite still requires the proxy target.
consumer_review: Audited exact IDs and ancestor selectors. Updated both direct SMA composite references and the policy-decrypt reference. Added the moved policy-path fact to the existing multi-app credential-theft unless list to preserve its previous suppression set. Rust and PHP consumers retain their original findings; new capabilities retain language scope. General hierarchy consumers do not turn neutral port/path references into attack facts.

focused_controls.includes: Three hostile PHP restoration fixtures, benign repair/query controls, renamed SMA exploit and local-admin/legacy-tag controls; same-path reassignment and argument-side-effect near misses; Rust crypto/keyring positives and API-name/comment negatives.

verification.offline_python_replay: Three mocked HTTP requests; not successful exploitation.

Three Python suspicious primitives became correctly located notable facts with identical matchers and scope. All three Python hostile findings and both original PHP hostile findings remain; PHP gained linked restored-file evaluation.
remaining_disagreements: Rust is judged BENIGN while atomscan remains SUSPICIOUS (0.98401093, L150). Accurate token/App-Bound boundary-crossing detections remain intentionally visible.

Python is judged MALICIOUS while atomscan changes from HOSTILE (0.99722624, L0) to BENIGN (0.9958473, L5000) after neutral rule corrections, despite retaining three hostile findings. This is a classifier miss; no inaccurate or duplicate trait was restored.
PHP changes from BENIGN (0.99094707, L5000) to HOSTILE (0.98, L25) after adding supported same-path staged evaluation. The original classifier miss is resolved for this specimen.
limitations: The model warns feature specification v18 versus extractor v21.
Source flow analysis reports explicit PHP/Python/Rust limitations; source, AST relationships and direct effects were reviewed instead of treating a clean flow query as absence.
External PHP payload bytes and the Python target list are unavailable. Actual deployment authorization and runtime success are unknown. No feed/scanner/advisory conviction was used as ground truth.
